sector_model: Insurance broker and risk services: organic growth, adjusted margin, fiduciary assets excluded from debt and cash, acquisition leverage, restructuring cash, pension. Not an insurer; no reserve model.
thesis: Aon plc (NYSE: AON), global insurance broker. Q3 2026 (10-Q 0001628280-26-067879 filed 2026-10-28): revenue 4,101M vs 3,997M (+2.6%), operating income 809M vs 816M, net income 476M vs 458M, diluted EPS 2.23 vs 2.11. 9M revenue 13,381M (+3.9%), operating income 3,439M, NI 2,239M (+11.8%), EPS 10.46 vs 9.21; restructuring (Accelerating Aon United) 281M in 9M, about 1.3B total program. TTM NI 3,932M (FY2025 3,695M + 9M26 - 9M25); OCF 3,574M, capex 308M, FCF 3,266M. Shares 212.157M (cover 2026-10-27), market cap 71.8B at 338.31: TTM P/E 18.3x, FCF yield 4.55%. Balance sheet moved sharply: total debt 28,041M at 2026-09-30 versus 15,249M at year end (13,404M of debt issued in 9M), cash 2,017M, equity 10.2B. Cause: 8-K 2026-08-31, agreement to buy USI Advantage Corp for 17B cash (merger agreement dated 2026-08-30; outside date 2026-06-01 extendable twice by three months; regulatory approvals). Press reports (not primary) state the price is about 14.5x synergized trailing EBITDA, financing by new debt, pro forma leverage about 4.5x and buybacks paused; the 10-Q shows no Q3 repurchases and 1.1B in H1. Market view: stock dropped about 7 to 10% on announcement; at 18x earnings it is cheaper than exchanges (CME 25.8x) but the earnings base excludes USI and the debt for it has already been raised in part. What the price assumes: successful integration and de-levering. Evidence for: EPS +14% in 9M, cash conversion 83% of NI. Against: organic growth not read, OCF 9M up only 4.5%.
counterthesis: Pro forma debt could reach about 45B including the 17B USI purchase (28.0B already, part may be pre-funded cash), against equity of 10.2B and TTM FCF of 3.3B; interest cost rises and buybacks stop, so per-share growth slows. Brokerage organic growth and margins depend on the P&C pricing cycle; softening rates cut commissions. Restructuring cash of about 1.2B is a recurring cost labelled one-time. USI price is 17B, and KKR's expected multiple return implies seller-favorable terms. The 2016 plane crash litigation is mentioned without amounts. Regulatory approval could delay or modify the deal. Not read: 10-Q MD&A (organic growth, adjusted margin), debt note maturity table, 10-K, Ex 99.1 and 99.2, financing 8-Ks of September; peers (MMC, WTW, BRO, AJG) not compared; shares 'outstanding' excludes any change since 2026-10-27.
invalidation: Thesis fails if organic growth falls below about 4%, pro forma leverage exceeds about 4.5x without a clear path down, free cash flow after interest does not cover dividends, or USI regulatory remedies or integration costs exceed plan.
